name: YouTube knowledge pipeline router (self-questioning conditional chain)
goal: Orchestrate the YouTube distillery as an explicit decision tree: the agent asks itself yes/no questions (env OK? transcript saved? video available? rate-limited? any track? which track rung? translation needed or failed? transcript usable? domain matched? gaps found?) and picks the matching skill next: topic search -> track-ladder fetch -> machine translation -> term graph -> gap check / KG merge -> distill + quality + novelty gates. Every question, answer, evidence and branch is logged. Delta vs generic agent routers or skill-chaining packs: the conditions are concrete YouTube transcript barriers (429/IP blocks, AI-dub tracks, tlang throttling, removed videos, disabled transcripts) with a logged branch for each, and ASR is never run automatically.
prerequisites: scripts/ensure_env.sh run at least once (.venv, .venv-translate, mcp-server/.venv)

inputs.name: video_ids_or_topic
inputs.description: One or more video ids, or --topic '<words>' [--langs en,de --max 3 --within year]

outputs.name: outcome
outputs.description: CANDIDATES_READY | COVERED | OFF_LEXICON | REJECT_thin_transcript | DEFER_rate_limited | STOP_video_unavailable | STOP_no_transcript_asr_flagged | STOP_translation_failed | STOP_env_broken

constraints: Transcript source is YouTube's Show transcript panel text (info section -> Transcript); say 'transcript', not 'captions'. Caption-file transports (.srt/.vtt) are only used internally and deleted.
Never invent transcript text, steps, or settings; every downstream fact must trace to a transcript timestamp.
No Whisper/ASR on the audio unless Matt explicitly asks; the router may only FLAG it as a last resort.
Each branch is a logged question with evidence; do not skip a question because the answer seems obvious.
DEFER rate-limited videos rather than hammering YouTube: let the backoff run, queue the id, and retry later (or Matt sets a proxy).
Outcome CANDIDATES_READY means outlines exist. Publishing still needs distill-transcript + quality_check_skill.py + novelty_check_skill.py, and the finance-risk rules for crypto/side-hustle.
Run with the pipeline venv: /workspace/skill-library/.venv/bin/python pipeline/route.py ...

steps.action: Q-search: was a topic given instead of ids? If yes, run youtube-topic-search-transcript-precheck (search_youtube_topics.py --precheck --require-transcript --skip-known) and take the top --max ids.

Q0: do youtube_transcript_api and yt_dlp import? If not, run scripts/ensure_env.sh and re-ask; if still broken, STOP_env_broken. Q1: is raw/<id>/meta.json ok with transcript.txt present (and no --refetch)? If yes, reuse it and jump to Q3.
steps.expect: Env healthy; fetch skipped when cached

steps.action: Q2: run youtube-show-transcript-track-ladder-fetch. On failure ask in order: Q2a unavailable/private/removed/age-gated -> STOP and drop; Q2b 429/IP-blocked after backoff -> DEFER to queue; Q2c no track at all -> STOP and flag ASR as a last resort for Matt to decide; Q2d translation failed/garbled -> STOP, original kept, suggest another backend.
steps.expect: English transcript, or a routed stop/defer with the reason

steps.action: Q3: does raw.txt have >= 150 words with [Music] markers under 5%? If not, REJECT_thin_transcript. Q4: is the English a translation (youtube-tlang or machine) or dub-derived? If yes, mark it so outlines carry translated_source and the distiller cross-checks transcript.orig.<lang>.txt.
steps.expect: Thin/music-only transcripts never reach distill; translations are labeled

steps.action: Q5/Q6: run transcript-domain-term-graph-extract. Is the best domain lexicon score >= 8? If not, flag OFF_LEXICON (extend pipeline/lexicons or use plain distill-transcript). Confirm graph.json has nodes and edges.

Q7: run knowledge-graph-gap-check-skill-outline. Are there candidate outlines? If yes, NEXT is distill-transcript on each outline's span, then quality_check_skill.py and novelty_check_skill.py; publish only what passes. If no, outcome COVERED (KG still updated). Write route.json and append route.jsonl.
steps.expect: Logged outcome per video; only gap-filling skills get distilled

verification: raw/<id>/route.json has decisions[] covering Q0..Q7 (or up to the stopping question) and an outcome
pipeline/logs/route.jsonl gains one line per routed video
Rate-limited ids show up in pipeline/queue/deferred.json, not as failures with invented text
